title: Attribution Guard
eyebrow: Proposal · keep Claude credit out of every repo you own

short.lead: Today the only guard is the house-rules hook, and it runs inside a session. It already stops my commits and pull request text from crediting Claude, but claude.ai adds its "Generated by Claude Code" footer on its own servers after the pull request is made, where no hook can reach. The 2026-10-08 attribution plan named a shared GitHub check as an optional last step, and it was never built; this page is that step, made required. GitHub cannot refuse text before it is saved, so the guarantee has to be at merge time: nothing that credits Claude can reach a repo's default branch. A GitHub Action checks every pull request, a ruleset makes that check required, and the same Action deletes the footer within seconds. It reuses the eight text patterns the hook already uses (hook.py, _ATTRIBUTION_TEXT_RES), so both guards agree on what counts.
short.hint: Tap a row to see what each part does and what it needs from you.
items: A required check reads every commit, the title and the description

It fails if any commit is authored or committed as Claude or from an anthropic.com address, or if a commit message, the pull request title or its description matches one of the eight patterns. It runs as pull_request_target, so it always runs the default branch's copy: a pull request cannot edit the check to make itself pass.
A ruleset on the default branch makes the check required

Every change must go through a pull request, the check must pass, force pushes and branch deletion are refused, and nobody is on the bypass list, you included. The check is pinned to the GitHub Actions app, so no other tool can post a fake pass.
Nothing from you, beyond the plan question under Choices.
Squash merges only, with the pull request title as the message

A normal merge commit's message is typed at merge time, after the check has run, so it is the one gap left. Squash with the title as the message means the merged text is exactly what the check already read.
The footer is deleted from descriptions and comments
The Action also runs when a description or comment is posted or edited, and removes any line matching the patterns. The footer can show for the few seconds before it runs; it can never be merged.
A push to the default branch is checked again
If anything ever reaches the default branch with Claude credit, the push run fails and GitHub emails you. This is a tripwire, not the guard: with the ruleset in place it should never fire.
One script installs it on every repo you own

tools/attribution_guard_install.py adds a short workflow file that calls the shared one in AjsClaudeCodeTools, then sets the ruleset and the merge setting through the GitHub API. It skips repos owned by other people, reports each repo's result, and is safe to re-run for new repos. Adding the file to each default branch is the one step that writes to all of them, so it waits for your approval.

changes: The one copy of the check logic, called by every repo.
Only the in-session hook checks attribution, and only for what I send.
Every pull request in every repo you own is checked on GitHub itself, whoever or whatever opened it.
A fix to the patterns lands in every repo at once. The patterns move into one file that hook.py and the workflow both read, so they cannot drift.
Adds the caller workflow, the ruleset and the squash-only setting to each repo, with a dry-run mode that lists what it would change.
One command covers every repo you own and can be re-run for new ones.
Tested first on focus-deck-app with a deliberate Claude-credited pull request, which must be refused, before it touches any other repo.
Default-branch ruleset and merge setting (each repo you own)
Turns the check from a warning into a block.
A failing check can still be merged, and merge commits carry whatever message is typed.
A Claude-credited change cannot merge, and the merged message is the checked title.
Merge commits and rebase merges are switched off on those repos.
choices: scope
Which repos should get the guard?
A
The 61 repos you own that are not forks
44 public and 17 private. Forks of other people's mods are left alone, since the workflow would show up in any pull request you send back upstream.
B
All 71 repos you own, forks included
Covers everything, at the cost of extra workflow files in the 10 forks.
Repos owned by other people or teams (8 of them) are never touched.
plan
Which GitHub plan is your account on?
A
Free
GitHub only enforces rulesets on public repos on Free. Your 17 private repos still get the check and the cleanup, but GitHub cannot stop a failing pull request merging there.
B
Pro or higher
Every repo, public and private, gets the full block.
GitHub's docs: rulesets need Pro or higher for private repos. I could not read your plan from here.
merge
How should pull requests merge?
A
Squash only, with the title as the message
Closes the last gap: the merged text is exactly what was checked.
B
Keep your current merge options
Merge commit messages are typed after the check runs, so a Claude line typed there would get through, and only the audit would catch it.
This changes how every merge in those repos looks in history.

wrapup.summary: A required GitHub check, enforced by a ruleset, that stops any Claude-credited change merging in the repos you own, plus automatic removal of the claude.ai footer.
wrapup.changing: Two new files in AjsClaudeCodeTools, then one small workflow file, a ruleset and a merge setting in each chosen repo.
wrapup.blocking: Your answers to the three choices.
wrapup.next: I build the check and the script, prove the block on focus-deck-app with a test pull request, then show you the dry-run list before anything touches the other repos.
